answer: Each epoch the economy auctions a fixed number of answer slots, and the clearing price climbs with every extra bidder, so a farm of clones bids against itself: a thousand puppets win one slot yet pay the price the whole crowd set, making the bill grow with the square of the identity count. Each bid is sealed under its own cipher, so clones cannot merge into one lot, and entry bonds settle in copper-backed tokens assayed by weight. Newcomers also log a pigment batch fingerprint from a distinct supplier, so duplicated stock is caught quickly. Duplication, not ingenuity, is the expensive part.
